summary.title: Non-idealities in CO2 electroreduction mechanisms revealed by automation-assisted kinetic analysis
summary.authors: Joy S Zeng, Vineet Padia, Joseph H Maalouf, Aditya M Limaye, Alexander H Liu, Michael A Yusov, Ian W Hunter, Karthish Manthiram
summary.executive_summary: This study addresses the limitations of traditional linearized kinetic analyses (Tafel and order dependence) in electrocatalysis, which often fail to capture complex reaction phenomena such as surface coverage effects and mixed control. The authors introduce a robotic system that automates the sequential testing of up to ten electrochemical cells, allowing for varied electrodes, electrolytes, gas compositions, and voltages. This automation facilitates cohesive kinetic analysis, a robust strategy requiring extensive data over wide reaction conditions. Using this platform, the team investigated the mechanism of CO2 electroreduction to carbon monoxide (CO) at immobilized metal tetrapyrroles: cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc), cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin (CoTPP), and iron phthalocyanine (FePc). The results reveal significant non-idealities in reaction rate data, specifically non-linear and potential-dependent bicarbonate and CO2 order dependences. For CoPc and CoTPP, bicarbonate inhibition is attenuated at more reductive potentials, consistent with models involving bicarbonate poisoning and potential-dependent mixed control. In contrast, FePc exhibits stronger bicarbonate inhibition at more reductive potentials, suggesting a different mechanism where the most abundant reactive intermediate is a species prior to the unoccupied site. The study demonstrates that complex mechanisms, unexplainable by standard Tafel analysis, are prevalent in this class of catalysts. The robotic workflow proved more time-efficient and reliable, with data correlating well with previous manual studies despite lower absolute rates. The work highlights the importance of considering electrolyte poisoning, coverage effects, and mixed control in interpreting CO2RR kinetics, suggesting that apparent contradictions in literature may stem from limited operating condition ranges. Future work will focus on incorporating membranes and automated mechanism enumeration to further standardize and accelerate electrocatalytic research.

claims.description: Automation enables robust cohesive kinetic analysis for electrocatalysis.
CO2RR at metal tetrapyrroles involves complex, non-linearizable mechanisms.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study addresses the limitations of traditional linearized kinetic analyses (Tafel and order dependence) in electrocatalysis, which often fail to capture complex reaction phenomena such as surface coverage effects and mixed control. The authors introduce a robotic system that automates the sequential testing of up to ten electrochemical cells, allowing for varied electrodes, electrolytes, gas compositions, and voltages. This automation facilitates cohesive kinetic analysis, a robust strategy requiring extensive data over wide reaction conditions. Using this platform, the team investigated the mechanism of CO2 electroreduction to carbon monoxide (CO) at immobilized metal tetrapyrroles: cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc), cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin (CoTPP), and iron phthalocyanine (FePc). The results reveal significant non-idealities in reaction rate data, specifically non-linear and potential-dependent bicarbonate and CO2 order dependences. For CoPc and CoTPP, bicarbonate inhibition is attenuated at more reductive potentials, consistent with models involving bicarbonate poisoning and potential-dependent mixed control. In contrast, FePc exhibits stronger bicarbonate inhibition at more reductive potentials, suggesting a different mechanism where the most abundant reactive intermediate is a species prior to the unoccupied site. The study demonstrates that complex mechanisms, unexplainable by standard Tafel analysis, are prevalent in this class of catalysts. The robotic workflow proved more time-efficient and reliable, with data correlating well with previous manual studies despite lower absolute rates. The work highlights the importance of considering electrolyte poisoning, coverage effects, and mixed control in interpreting CO2RR kinetics, suggesting that apparent contradictions in literature may stem from limited operating condition ranges. Future work will focus on incorporating membranes and automated mechanism enumeration to further standardize and accelerate electrocatalytic research.

Research Context
Traditional electrocatalysis kinetics rely on linearized rate data. These methods assume independent factorization of voltage and concentration. Complex phenomena like coverage effects break these assumptions. Cohesive kinetic analysis offers a more robust alternative. This approach requires large datasets over wide conditions. Manual data collection is slow and error-prone. Existing automation focuses on high-throughput screening. Miniaturization limits product quantification for kinetic analysis. Parallelization often lacks individual online product detection. Sequential testing with online quantification is ideal.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to automate electrochemical rate data collection. The robotic system accommodates varied experimental parameters. The primary goal is to investigate CO2RR mechanisms. Specific catalysts include CoPc, CoTPP, and FePc. The hypothesis is that non-idealities are prevalent. These non-idealities manifest as changing order dependences. The authors predict complex mechanisms explain these trends. Phenomena like electrolyte poisoning are expected to be key. The study seeks to reconcile conflicting literature reports. It is hypothesized that standard Tafel analysis is insufficient.

Methodological Details
CoPc catalysts were drop-casted onto Toray060 carbon paper. CoPc loading was 5.98 x 10^-11 mol/cm2. CoTPP and FePc used carbon black-containing DMF. CoTPP loading was 5.11 x 10^-10 mol/cm2. FePc loading was 8.04 x 10^-10 mol/cm2. Electrolytes were prepared from Na2CO3 and NaClO4 stocks. Stock solutions were bubbled overnight with CO2. Final electrolytes had 1 mol/L ionic strength. Electrolyses were queued in batches of ten. A leak-free Ag/AgCl reference electrode was used. The reference electrode was calibrated daily. Data was uploaded to an SQL database. A python script processed the data files. The robot houses a single cell body. Ten cell pan pairs house working electrodes. The cell body moves horizontally and vertically. Online product quantification used a gas chromatograph. The working electrode exposed a 10 mm diameter circle. A 0.25 mm platinum wire counter electrode was used.

Procedures And Architectures
The robot sequentially tests each cell pan. Electrolyte is pumped through the 'electrolyte in' port. Gas flow is initiated before voltage application. Voltage is applied after a few minutes. Online detection of CO and H2 occurs. Electrolyte is pumped out via 'electrolyte out' tubing. Cell body cleaning uses a wash station. MilliQ water is pumped for cleaning cycles. The cell body is rinsed after ten electrolyses. The setup is a three-electrode, undivided compartment cell. No membrane separates anode and cathode. Oxygen crossover can cause parasitic ORR current. Average Faradaic efficiency closure was ~60%. Pt counter electrode prevents anode product attribution. High HER Faradaic efficiencies were observed. CO2 was bubbled into the electrolyte. Currents were below mass transport limits.

Key Results
Newly measured CO rates were up to ten times lower. Faradaic efficiencies toward CO were typically under 30%. Previous kinetic trends in CO production were preserved. New data correlated well with previous work. Non-ideal mechanisms showed curvature in data. Bicarbonate inhibition was voltage-dependent for all catalysts. CoPc and CoTPP showed negative bicarbonate dependence at less reductive potentials. CoPc and CoTPP showed positive dependence at more reductive potentials. FePc showed greater bicarbonate inhibition at more reductive potentials. CoPc CO2 order dependence appeared ideal and first order. CoTPP CO2 order was slightly below one. CoTPP CO2 order decreased at more reductive potentials. FePc CO2 order was more attenuated at less reductive potentials. FePc CO2 order curves intersected at low pressures. Voltage inhibited the reaction at low CO2 pressures for FePc.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
CoPc and CoTPP mechanisms involve bicarbonate poisoning. These mechanisms also involve potential-dependent mixed control. Poisoning is described by positive electrosorption valency. FePc mechanism involves a species prior to the unoccupied site. This explains the contrasting bicarbonate trend in FePc. On-cycle poisoning species can also explain trends. Complex mechanisms are prevalent in metal tetrapyrroles. Standard Tafel analysis misses these complexities. Literature contradictions may arise from limited condition ranges. Automation enables robust cohesive kinetic analysis.

Contradictions And Limitations
The undivided cell design allows oxygen crossover. This leads to incomplete Faradaic efficiency closure. High HER Faradaic efficiencies were observed. Pt deposition might affect HER sites. Bubbling CO2 may influence measured kinetics. New rates were lower than previously reported. Models only qualitatively capture observed trends. Models do not quantitatively fit all data. Specific reaction mechanisms were not definitively proposed. The study relies on conceptual and generalized analyses.

Claims
Automation enables robust cohesive kinetic analysis for electrocatalysis. The robotic system automates sequential testing. It accommodates varied experimental conditions. Data collection is more time-efficient. The undivided cell design has limitations. Oxygen crossover affects Faradaic efficiency. This approach can reveal complex mechanisms. It standardizes and accelerates data collection.
CO2RR at metal tetrapyrroles involves complex, non-linearizable mechanisms. Bicarbonate order dependences change with potential. CO2 order dependences are non-linear. These trends are unexplainable by standard models. CoPc CO2 order appeared ideal. Standard Tafel analysis is insufficient. Electrolyte poisoning and mixed control are key.

Data And Code Availability
All experimental data is available as xlsx. Supporting information includes protocols and data. The work is licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Data robustness was evaluated against literature precedent. New data correlated well with previous work. Kinetic trends were preserved despite lower rates. Models were tested for goodness-of-fit. Some models could not fit observed trends.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the robot design and cell assembly. Figure 2 illustrates bicarbonate dependence and mechanisms. Figure 3 shows CO2 dependence and mechanisms. Figure S5 shows Faradaic efficiency closure. Figure S7 compares new and previous kinetic trends. Figure S8 shows correlation with previous data. Figure S10 shows Faradaic efficiencies toward CO and H2.

Three Takeaways
1. A robotic system automates electrochemical kinetic data collection. 2. CO2RR at metal tetrapyrroles exhibits complex, non-linear kinetics. 3. Future work will improve automation and mechanism enumeration.
